title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles of categories M, N and O with regard to braking

paragraphs.title: Scope
paragraphs.text: Scope This Regulation applies to vehicles of categories M2, M3, N and O with regard to braking.

paragraphs.title: Vehicles of categories M2 and M3
paragraphs.text: Vehicles of categories M2 and M3 In the case of vehicles of categories M2 and M3, the braking requirements set out in Annex 4 shall apply.

paragraphs.title: Definitions
paragraphs.text: Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply:

paragraphs.title: Braking system
paragraphs.text: Braking system "Braking system" means the combination of parts whose function is to progressively reduce the speed of a moving vehicle, bring it to a halt, or keep it stationary if it is already halted; these functions are specified in paragraph 5.1. Figure 1 - Basic braking system schematic Brake Pedal Master Cylinder Caliper Figure 1: Schematic representation of a basic hydraulic braking system

paragraphs.title: Service braking system
paragraphs.text: Service braking system "Service braking system" means the braking system which allows the driver to control the movement of the vehicle and bring it to a halt safely, quickly and effectively, whatever its conditions of loading.

paragraphs.title: Secondary braking system
paragraphs.text: Secondary braking system "Secondary braking system" means the braking system which allows the driver to halt the vehicle in the event of failure of the service braking system.

paragraphs.title: Parking braking system
paragraphs.text: Parking braking system "Parking braking system" means the braking system which allows the vehicle to be held stationary on an inclined surface even in the absence of the driver.

paragraphs.title: Endurance braking system
paragraphs.text: Endurance braking system "Endurance braking system" means a supplementary braking system able to stabilize vehicle speed over a long downhill section. Table 1 - Braking performance requirements

paragraphs.title: General requirements
paragraphs.text: General requirements Every vehicle shall be equipped with a braking system which shall comply with the requirements set out in Annex 4.

paragraphs.title: Functions of braking systems
paragraphs.text: Functions of braking systems The braking system of every vehicle shall fulfil the following functions: (a) service braking, enabling the movement of the vehicle to be controlled     and the vehicle to be brought to a halt safely, quickly and effectively; (b) secondary braking, enabling the vehicle to be brought to a halt in the     event of failure of the service braking system; (c) parking braking, enabling the vehicle to be held stationary on a gradient; (d) endurance braking, where fitted, to stabilize speed on long downhill sections.

paragraphs.title: Braking surfaces
paragraphs.text: Braking surfaces The braking systems prescribed in paragraph 5.1 shall be so designed that they act on braking surfaces permanently connected to the wheels through components of adequate strength. Where braking effort on an axle is provided by the engine or an electric motor, a disconnect device shall be permitted. Table 2 - ABS requirements by vehicle category
